seo.title: Teleprompter Guides: Setup, Scripts & Natural Delivery
seo.description: Browse practical teleprompter guides for choosing a workflow, writing scripts, setting up your camera, reading naturally, and fixing common mistakes.

hero.alt: Camera, laptop teleprompter, microphone, and notebook in a creator recording setup

content.html: Use this collection to decide whether a teleprompter fits your workflow, prepare a script, set up the camera and reading area, deliver the script naturally, choose a scrolling method, and fix common problems.
Start with the problem you have now. You do not need to read the guides in order.

If you need to shape the message before you format it for a teleprompter, start with Script Writing for Speaking. It covers the audience, outline, draft, timing, and format-specific templates; return here for setup and reading delivery.
Decide whether a teleprompter is appropriate for your recording, teaching, webinar, presentation, or public-speaking workflow.
Compare delivery methods by accuracy, preparation, flexibility, production style, and use case.
Turn written prose into a spoken script using conversational wording, shorter sentences, meaningful line breaks, pauses, and clear emphasis.

content.text: [How to Set Up a Teleprompter Without Special Hardware](/blog/teleprompter-setup-without-hardware/)

content.html: Build a practical browser setup with a laptop, external webcam, phone, tablet, or separate camera before deciding whether you need a beam-splitter rig.
Reduce distracting eye movement, avoid robotic pacing, read phrases instead of isolated words, and rehearse with the actual camera setup.
Compare voice-assisted, fixed-speed, manual, and remote control based on pauses, timing, noise, improvisation, and production risk.
Diagnose problems with text width, camera position, script language, scrolling, recognition, font size, rehearsal, and backup controls.

content.text: Speaking on camera beyond the teleprompter

content.html: Use the broader speaking-on-camera collection for confidence practice, visual and vocal delivery, camera eye contact, and pre-recorded presentations. These skills apply whether you use a full script, bullet points, or no teleprompter.
These editorial guides explain decisions, principles, and workflows.
For instructions on adding a script, selecting a scroll mode, adjusting the reading view, enabling Notch Mode, using Remote Control, and recording, use the SolPrompter product guide.
For a feature-by-feature product overview, read SolPrompter AI Teleprompter: Features Tested.

SolPrompter publishes this guide collection and develops the product referenced in it. Editorial guides distinguish first-party product documentation from independent research and professional guidance.
